What Safari Reading List marketing is — save-for-later, not Reader Mode

Western indie listings often show one or more of these Reading List surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Save to Reading List (保存到阅读列表) — toolbar button, share-sheet action, or in-app browser menu that queues the current webpage into Safari Reading List
  • Add to Reading List (添加到阅读列表) — share extension or Safari action sheet marketing that names the add-to-queue gesture buyers recognize on iPhone and iPad
  • Reading List sidebar (阅读列表) — Safari sidebar or bookmarks-adjacent collection showing saved articles grouped for later reading
  • Saved articles for later (稍后阅读) — gallery frames that emphasize the read-later queue outcome — articles waiting until the buyer has time
  • Offline saved pages (离线阅读) — when your English listing claims saved Reading List articles remain readable without a live connection
  • Ultra Reading List branding — when your en-US listing uses Ultra Reading List or premium-tier read-later branding as the hero story on supported devices

Reading List saves the page for later. Reader Mode restyles the page for distraction-free reading now. Your gallery may show both on adjacent frames — zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame. A Save to Reading List share-sheet capture is not a Reader Mode typography demo, not a Tab Groups grid, and not a generic Safari tab bar unless that is what the screenshot depicts.

How is Safari Reading List different from Reader Mode?

Reading List is a save-for-later queue — Save to Reading List, saved articles you open later, 阅读列表. Reader Mode is distraction-free article restyle — clean typography, stripped ads, 阅读器模式.
